note: lxpt relay core v1 (spec/floor-v1.md section 5). Generated by python/gen_core_fixtures.py from the Python reference; every value is a TEST value and every signature a filler (the host verifies before the core sees a CLAIM or RELEASE). Each scenario builds one Relay (relay_hash, limits, talk_limit_s) and runs its steps in order: 'do' is admit, client, peer, tick, leg_down, peer_up, peer_rtt or peer_down; 'at' is the clock in ms; 'hex' the bytes received; 'rx' when they were received if not 'at'. 'expect' is every line the step produced, in order: 'admit ok|no' for an admit, 'send c<leg>|p<peer> <hex>' and 'note <channel tag> <floor action>'. Scenarios named sim_R<n> are traces recorded at relay n of python/sim.py's fixture run. A 'ticks' step is a run of 'count' ticks 'every' ms apart from 'at', none of which produced a line.

scenarios.name: one_relay_spurt
scenarios.note: SUBs, a CLAIM forwarded, granted, frames to voice legs only, a duplicate dropped, HEARD upstream, RELEASE forwarded, heartbeats

scenarios.name: narrow_leg_profile
scenarios.note: a BLE leg makes the spurt Codec2 and gets its frames; an Opus spurt skips it

scenarios.name: admission_rate_limit
scenarios.note: two new claims per client leg per second, so junk on one leg blocks only that leg; retries pass; stale ones are dropped

scenarios.name: emergency_rate_limit
scenarios.note: one Emergency claim per identity per channel per 10 s

scenarios.name: busy_yield_carry_the_claim
scenarios.note: BUSY and YIELD are preceded by the holder's CLAIM

scenarios.name: peers
scenarios.note: peer up, PEER summaries with split horizon, a remote claim and its TALKING, frames both ways, TALKING forwarded at most once a second, peer lost after 15 s

scenarios.name: late_joiners
scenarios.note: a leg or a peer that newly lists a channel with a live spurt gets its CLAIM and TALKING

scenarios.name: leases
scenarios.note: a SUB lease runs 60 s; a released leg goes at once; an empty channel is freed

scenarios.name: stale_frames_count_as_heard
scenarios.note: a frame older than 500 ms is not forwarded but still counts as heard

scenarios.name: late_frames_by_media_time
scenarios.note: a live spurt's frames more than 800 ms behind its schedule (seq x 60 ms after its earliest) are a backlog: not forwarded, though they count as heard; late frames arriving at real-time pace are a talker whose numbering shifted, and five of them re-anchor the schedule

scenarios.name: lost_backlog_in_window_does_not_resume
scenarios.note: a backlog received inside the resume window, seconds behind its spurt's schedule, does not bring the lost spurt back and is not forwarded; the spurt ends with the window (v1.2)

scenarios.name: lost_resumes_on_schedule
scenarios.note: inside the resume window, after a dropped backlog frame, a frame on its spurt's schedule brings the lost spurt back and is forwarded (v1.2)

scenarios.name: yielded_backlog_does_not_resume
scenarios.note: a local spurt pre-empted (yielded, never lost) whose talker's backlog arrives 6.3 s behind after the winner released: not resumed, not forwarded; the next frame on schedule resumes it (v1.2)

scenarios.name: settle_from_peer_rtt
scenarios.note: the settle window is the largest RTT of peers on the channel, capped at 300 ms

scenarios.name: garbage_and_misdirected
scenarios.note: undecodable bytes and messages on the wrong side are ignored

scenarios.name: small_tables
scenarios.note: channels, spurts and dedup at their limits

scenarios.name: frames_only_from_their_source
scenarios.note: a client cannot move a floor with a forged FRAME: a local spurt's frames count only from its talker's leg, a remote spurt's only from a peer

scenarios.name: bench_2026_11_04
scenarios.note: the bench failure at a relay: a backlog 13 s after the loss neither takes the floor from the live talker nor is forwarded; the dead spurt's talker gets the holder's CLAIM and a YIELD

scenarios.name: stale_evidence_never_promotes
scenarios.note: a FRAME or TALKING queued through a pass (older than 500 ms) does not make a pending or known spurt live: after a relay's own stall, a backlog is not a talker

scenarios.name: stale_frames_and_foreign_legs
scenarios.note: a stale frame of a live local spurt still counts as heard, and one of a lost spurt received inside the window still resumes it (neither is forwarded); a frame naming an ended local spurt from another client leg gets no YIELD, its talker's own leg does

scenarios.name: yield_again_while_the_talker_sends
scenarios.note: a yielded local talker that keeps sending gets the YIELD again, at most once a second

scenarios.name: unmatched_release_and_heard
scenarios.note: a RELEASE that matches no record is not forwarded and moves no counter; it still blocks its own CLAIM; a HEARD for it goes nowhere

scenarios.name: release_repeat_forwarded_once
scenarios.note: the talker's second RELEASE copy is forwarded once more (a single loss downstream does not cost the listener's HEARD); a third copy, or one from another leg, is not (v1.3)

scenarios.name: release_repeat_from_the_claims_peer
scenarios.note: a remote spurt's repeat RELEASE is forwarded once when it comes from the peer its claim came from; the same copy echoed by another peer is not, so no loop forms (v1.3)

scenarios.name: release_repeat_after_a_lost_spurt
scenarios.note: a spurt that ended lost here is not ended by a late RELEASE, and the RELEASE is not forwarded: only a spurt a RELEASE ended has a repeat to forward (v1.3)
